chunks: But they split up the order among themselves; (yet) all of them have to come back to Me.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about the fragmentation of religious communities and their ultimate return to God?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the fragmentation of religious authority and the proliferation of divergent sects (firaq) as a sign of spiritual deviation, contrasting human disunity with divine unity. It underscores the inevitability of the final return (ruju') to Allah for individual accountability, a concept deeply tied to the Shia understanding of the Hereafter and the role of the Ahl al-Bayt as the unifying guide. The verse serves as a reminder that despite earthly divisions, ultimate judgment rests solely with God, who will assess each soul's adherence to the true path.
